question: Should OpenClaw commit this publisher-feed trust contract now, while its producer PRs and RFC remain open, or wait for the producer format and real interoperability proof to stabilize?
rationale: The patch establishes which externally signed publisher data core will trust and reuses an existing install-catalog verification path; tests cannot determine whether that cross-repository contract is the intended permanent security boundary.

options.title: Stabilize then merge
options.body: Wait for the producer/RFC contract to settle and require actual ClawHub query, change, and reset artifacts to pass this exact head before merge.

options.title: Accept provisional contract
options.body: Merge the verifier as an intentionally provisional foundation and explicitly own possible follow-up compatibility changes across the stacked PRs.

options.title: Land DSSE foundation only
options.body: Land the narrower standard-envelope compatibility PR first and defer publisher projection types until the producer contract is independently proven.

recommendation.title: Stabilize then merge
recommendation.body: Wait for the producer/RFC contract to settle and require actual ClawHub query, change, and reset artifacts to pass this exact head before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans core plugin architecture, compatibility, and the permanent boundary for trusting marketplace publisher data.
